title: Sebastian and the Clock
premise: In 1859, on a storm-battered coast, lighthouse keeper August Crane keeps the light burning while the army arrives to requisition the harbor town and seize the shipping ledger that holds every family's name, debts, and loyalties. When evacuation berths are announced for only a handful of townsfolk before the great storms make landfall, August discovers his late wife's brother is among the officers enforcing the requisition — and that the ledger could either condemn or save the found-family of drifters, orphans, and outcasts who have become his true household. Forced to choose which name gets the last berth, August steals the ledger, trades his own place for theirs, and holds the light through the worst night of the storms so the rescue ship can find the harbor. He survives, half-drowned and stripped of his post, but the town's scattered survivors return in spring to rebuild around him — no longer keeper of the light, but keeper of each other.
about_author: Oscar Hartwell is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs and requisition records from nineteenth-century coastal towns. Hartwell writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of official decisions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: August Crane polishes the lamp, counts his stores, and measures his life in what can be carried. His household — orphaned Tilly, old sailor Bram, and runaway clerk Nell — gathers for supper as the first storm warnings fly. POV: August. Emotional beat: quiet contentment shadowed by the season's first unease.

chapters.title: Gray Sails at Dawn
chapters.summary: An army cutter anchors in the harbor; soldiers march ashore with requisition orders signed in London. August watches from the gallery as the town's boats are impounded. POV: August. Emotional beat: dread arriving with the tide.

chapters.title: Names in a Ledger
chapters.summary: Captain Ellery Vane, August's dead wife's brother, announces the army will take the shipping ledger holding every family's record. Nell, whose forged papers live in its pages, panics. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: terror of exposure.

chapters.title: What the Orders Say
chapters.summary: Vane visits the lighthouse under pretense of inspection; the estranged in-laws circle each other with grief and grievance. He mentions evacuation berths for 'essential persons' before the great storms. POV: August. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: Tilly Counts the Berths
chapters.summary: Tilly learns there are five berths for their household of six and begins secretly bargaining with neighbors, revealing how many families will be left behind. POV: Tilly. Emotional beat: a child confronting arithmetic of abandonment.

chapters.title: Bram's Confession
chapters.summary: Old Bram admits he once served under Vane and deserted after a botched evacuation that drowned thirty souls — the very precedent for this one. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: shame transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Requisition Ball
chapters.summary: At an officers' reception, August pleads for more berths; Vane refuses publicly, and August glimpses the ledger unguarded on a trestle table. POV: August. Emotional beat: humiliation hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Nell's Name
chapters.summary: A soldier cross-references the ledger and nearly finds Nell's alias; she decides to flee alone rather than endanger the household. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice born of guilt.

chapters.title: Storm Glass Falling
chapters.summary: Barometers plunge; the great storm's vanguard strips shingles and floods the low streets. The army accelerates the evacuation timetable by three days. POV: August. Emotional beat: time collapsing.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Vane offers August a berth if he surrenders the names of 'undesirables' hiding in town. August refuses and realizes the final berth must go to someone — and everyone looks to him to choose. POV: August. Emotional beat: the weight of judgment.

chapters.title: Tilly Runs
chapters.summary: Believing herself the obvious cut, Tilly stows away on a supply wagon bound inland and disappears into the gathering gale. POV: Tilly. Emotional beat: fear mistaken for sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ledger Night
chapters.summary: August, Bram, and Nell steal into the requisition house during the blackout and take the ledger, tearing out pages to protect the town's hidden names. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: theft as an act of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Hunted Through Rain
chapters.summary: Soldiers sweep the town for the missing ledger; Bram is arrested covering their tracks and refuses to talk under questioning. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: endurance as loyalty.

chapters.title: Vane's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Vane confronts August at the light: the ledger for Bram's freedom and a berth for all — except whoever stole it. August sees his brother-in-law is himself trapped by orders from above. POV: August. Emotional beat: recognizing the enemy's chains.

chapters.title: Found in the Dunes
chapters.summary: August and Nell find Tilly half-frozen in a fisherman's hut; she confesses she ran so the others could live. They carry her home through the rising sea. POV: Tilly. Emotional beat: found family affirmed in the worst weather.

chapters.title: The Choice Made
chapters.summary: With one berth left, August writes his own name last and gives it away — to a dying neighbor's widow no one else claimed — sealing his fate to stay through the storm. POV: August. Emotional beat: surrender as strength.

chapters.title: The Great Storm Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: The evacuation ship loads at dawn in mountainous seas; the household is separated as August remains ashore with the light. Vane, disobeying orders, stays behind with him. POV: August. Emotional beat: farewell without goodbye.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Light
chapters.summary: Through the storm's black heart, August and Vane fight to keep the lamp lit as waves breach the tower; Vane confesses he requested this posting to find his sister's husband. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: reconciliation forged in shared peril.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Meridian
chapters.summary: A transport founders on the shoals; August turns the light toward the wreck and guides survivors to the harbor through the night, the ledger's knowledge of the channels proving decisive. POV: August. Emotional beat: the stolen book saving lives.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Salt
chapters.summary: Dawn reveals the drowned and the saved; the army withdraws, discredited. Vane reports the ledger destroyed and lets August go free, then departs without forgiveness asked or given. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: justice done quietly, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Spring Return
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the evacuated townsfolk trickle back; Tilly, Nell, and Bram return to find August rebuilding the light unpaid and unofficial. The torn ledger pages are read aloud and burned, debts forgiven. POV: Tilly. Emotional beat: homecoming.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: On the first clear night, August lights the lamp again — not by commission, but by consent of the people it guides. The household gathers in the watch room, and he finally stops measuring what can be carried. POV: August. Emotional beat: belonging beyond office, identity chosen rather than assigned.
